summary: Arnold J. Toynbee worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Winchester College (~1902–1907) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1907–1911), later holding posts at King's College London (~1919–1924), Chatham House (~1925–1955), and the London School of Economics (~1925–1955).

Arnold Kunst worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and University of Warsaw under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak, Stanisław Schayer, and Erich Frauwallner, later teaching at Lviv, SOAS, and Cambridge.

Arsène Darmesteter was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the École des chartes, INALCO, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Gaston Paris, later holding posts at the EPHE, Paris, and ENS.

Artemij Keidan is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at Sapienza University of Rome (2001–2005), lectured at the University of L'Aquila (2009–2010), and became an Associate Professor at Sapienza in 2020.

Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller, and Leipzig under Rudolf von Roth. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1880–1899).

Arthur Berriedale Keith worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Julius Eggeling at Edinburgh and Arthur Anthony Macdonell at Oxford. He served in the Colonial Office and lectured in history at the University of Edinburgh (1914–1944).

Arthur Christensen worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Johannes Edvard Lehmann and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later serving as docent at Copenhagen (1919–1945).

Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at King's College London and under Theodor Goldstücker, Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and Heinrich August Jäschke. He served in the Indian Civil Service from 1860.
Arthur Evans was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Harrow School (~1866–1870) and Brasenose College (1870), and later taught John Marshall.
Arthur F. Buehler works in religious studies and Indology. He studied under Annemarie Schimmel and held a post at Victoria University of Wellington.

Arthur F. Wright worked in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard under John King Fairbank, later holding faculty posts at Stanford (1947, 1958) and Yale University (1959, 1961).
Arthur Galletti was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He was educated at Cheltenham College and Trinity College, Oxford (~1895–1899), and served in the Indian Civil Service from 1900 to 1934.
Arthur Haberlandt worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He succeeded Michael Haberlandt in 1924 and held a post at the University of Vienna from ~1914 to 1945.

Arthur Henry Ewing worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Washington & Jefferson College, Pittsburgh Theological Seminary, and Johns Hopkins. He headed the Christian Boys' Boarding School and Ewing Christian College, and was a fellow at Allahabad.

Arthur Henry Fox Strangways was a scholar in Indology and other fields. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford, and the Berlin University of the Arts, later serving as a schoolmaster at Dulwich College (1884–1886) and Wellington College (1886–1910).
Arthur James Beattie was a linguist who studied at Montrose Academy, the University of Aberdeen (~1931–1935), and the University of Cambridge (~1935–1939). He taught William Sidney Allen.

Arthur Leslie Saunders was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1880–1883), and held posts in the Indian Civil Service (1880) and the India Office (1918–1923).

Arthur Llewellyn Basham was a historian and Indologist. He studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett, and held posts at SOAS (1948–1965), the Australian National University (1965–1979), the University of Toronto (1978), and The Asiatic Society (1985).
Arthur Marshman Spencer was an Indologist who completed his studies at Kingswood School and Headingley College.
Arthur Mason Tippetts Jackson worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1884–1888) and served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1888 to 1909.
